title: Hosted API onramp scripts & pricing deltas
content:
Purpose:
Quick, actionable materials for two things we keep hearing from developers: (1) they want rapid proof-of-value in minutes, and (2) pricing language that maps clearly to engineering tradeoffs. This doc bundles short onramp scripts (landing copy, README quickstart snippet, in-product onboarding email) plus three pricing-language variants and compact competitive notes so PMs/marketing can iterate quickly.

Audience:
- Product marketing and growth for website/CTA copy
- Dev relations and docs for quickstart snippets
- Sales engineering for starter pitch language

High-level positioning thesis (one sentence):
"The simplest, predictable way for engineers to ship LLM features: fast local-to-hosted onramp, transparent unit economics, and pragmatic defaults tuned for production."

Developer-first value props (short bullets to use across channels):
- Zero-guess latency and cost: transparent per-token profiling and latency SLO badges so engineers can pick a config that matches SLAs.
- Quick confidence: a 3-line quickstart that returns a streaming response from a curated model in under five minutes.
- Production defaults, not research defaults: vectors, KV caching, and batching enabled with safe defaults that reduce token spend without surprise quality regressions.
- Portable rollout: same API surface for hosted, dedicated, or private deployments so teams can prototype on hosted and scale safely.
- Diagnostic-first observability: per-request traces, token cost breakdowns, and guided troubleshooting steps surfaced in Console and APIs.

Onramp scripts (copyable snippets):
1) Landing hero (30–40 chars + subline):
Hero: "Start serving smarter responses in minutes."
Subline: "Three-line quickstart, predictable pricing, and production defaults built for engineers. No surprises—just latency and cost you can reason about."
CTA: "Try it free — 10k free tokens"

2) README quickstart (short code block for GitHub):
"Install SDK, set API_KEY, call client.generate with prompt; streaming sample included. Example shows 6–8 lines of code and a link to 'Inspect cost breakdown' post-response."
Include small note: "Try the `--latency-slo` flag to auto-select a lower-latency model variant."

3) In-product onboarding email (subject + 3 bullets):
Subject: "Your Redwood hosted API credits — get a sample in 5 min"
Body bullets:
- One-click sample app that streams a response and shows token cost.
- Auto-detects a default model variant for sub-200ms replies for chat-like prompts.
- Toggle a 'cost saver' mode to see 30–50% savings with quantized variants.

Pricing-language drafts (three variants — pick one direction per channel):
A. Engineer-centric, explicit units (recommended for docs & API pages):
- "Pay per token processed (input + output). Example: a 100-token prompt + 400-token response = 500 billed tokens. Unit price: $X per 1k tokens."
- "Committed reserved capacity: fixed monthly commit for Dedicated with a guaranteed throughput tier and 12% discount on per-token rates."
- "Free developer credits: 10k tokens on signup; free for prototyping only (no SLA)."

B. Outcome-oriented packaging (recommended for sales/landing):
- "Starter: free credits + pay-as-you-go per 1k tokens for prototyping."
- "Scale: committed capacity with predictable monthly spend and a 'burst' buffer for traffic spikes."
- "Enterprise: private plane & SLA, billed as platform + usage banding."

C. Hybrid simplicity (UI tooltip language):
- "Pay per token. Switch model or enable 'cost saver' to reduce unit price; we show estimated cost before you send requests."
- Tooltips: "Estimated monthly: $X based on 100k tokens/month on current model + batching enabled."

Pricing callouts & guardrails (copy snippets for docs):
- "We charge for both input and output tokens to keep behaviour predictable. Your Console shows per-request token breakdown and historical unit cost so you can tune prompts."
- "Batching and prefix/KV caching significantly lower billed tokens — see 'Optimize' tab for model-specific recommendations."

Competitive analysis — quick notes and messaging consequences (1-paragraph bullets):
- General cloud AI endpoints: they hide cost levers and often surface opaque throughput. Message: emphasize our transparent per-token profiles and 'latency SLO' tuning as a differentiator.
- LLM API incumbents (simplicity-first): they win on frictionless access. Message: lead with 'simple first minute' (3-line quickstart) and then nudge to our production controls.
- Inference infra vendors/self-hosted runtimes: they sell control at cost of setup complexity. Message: we combine the best of both: start hosted for speed, then lift to Dedicated/Private with the same API and tooling.

Objection handling (short scripts for SDRs/PMMs):
- 'We're worried about unpredictably high bills': show Console token breakdown and recommend committed baseline + burst buffer.
- 'I need <100ms latency': show model variant and region routing + SLO guarantees in Dedicated tiers.
- 'Compliance requires private infrastructure': outline Private offering + migration checklist (networking, KMS keys).

Experiment ideas (A/B testable copy & metrics):
- Hero variants: "Start in 5 min" vs "Ship a feature in a day" — metric: signup -> first API call time, activation rate.
- Pricing phrasing: explicit per-token math vs outcome packaging — metric: conversion to trial + requests per trial.
- Quickstart CTA: 'Try it free — 10k tokens' vs 'Run a sample in 1 click' — metric: sample-run rate and dropoff in code snippet.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Exact per-1k token amounts (product to confirm rates and committed discount bands).
- Free-tier size: 10k vs 25k tokens — tradeoff between experience and abuse.
- Whether to surface 'cost-saver' toggle in the initial quickstart or behind a 'try optimizations' step.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- PM (Marco) to lock per-token pricing ranges and committed discount bands (due: 2025-11-10).
- DevRel (Ellen) to prepare 3-line README and sandbox app for embedded landing (due: 2025-11-12).
- Growth (Aisha) to run hero A/B test in the next website release (due: 2025-11-20).

Appendix — short sample handoff copy for support articles (one-liners):
- 'How tokens map to your bill' — quick explainer + example.
- 'How to pick a model for latency-sensitive apps' — checklist with region and batching tips.
- 'Switching from hosted to Dedicated' — migration checklist and expected lead times.

Document history: created as a consolidated working brief combining product, devrel, and growth input. This doc is intentionally succinct so teams can lift snippets directly.

End of brief.
